releases.title: Tabs for every phone
releases.summary: Open as many phones and second screens as you like as tabs in one window, pop any of them out into a phone-shaped window, and find Settings in a tab of its own. The phone app gets the same new look.
mac: Every phone and second screen you mirror opens as a tab in the main window, with no limit. Each tab keeps its own connection, so switching tabs never restarts a mirror.
Mobile view (⇧⌘M) pops a tab out into its own phone-shaped window. New window still opens separate windows.
Device shortcuts, ⌘K and clipboard history act on the tab in front.
Settings opens as a tab next to your phones.
phoneApp: A new look to match the Mac: refined dark and light colours, the system font, small corners and blue buttons and switches.
Home, Device and Settings sit in a tab bar at the bottom, above a blue status bar that shows which Mac you're linked to.

releases.title: Room for the mirror
releases.summary: Fixes the mirror being squeezed into a narrow column when the side bar floats over it.
mac: With a floating side bar, the mirror, tab and controls fill the window again instead of a narrow column on the left.
The floating side bar stops above the status bar.
Breadcrumbs no longer run into the phone controls in narrow windows.
phoneApp: No changes in this release: 0.8.2 is still the current phone app.

releases.title: A familiar workbench
releases.summary: Twinglass for Mac has a new workbench: an activity bar, an explorer for your phones, the phone as a tab and a status bar that shows what's live.
mac: A new workbench: a title bar with a command center that opens the palette, and an activity bar for Phones, opening an app, clipboard history, second screens, Agents, shortcuts and Settings.
Phones sit in an explorer-style tree: one row per way to reach the phone (USB, Wi-Fi), with an inline Mirror button, or double-click.
The mirrored phone is an editor tab (close it to disconnect), with breadcrumbs and the phone's controls underneath.
A status bar with a blue phone indicator and the stream's resolution, frame rate, codec, latency and audio.
New light and dark colours, the system font, square corners and a blue accent across every dialog and menu.
The compact, phone-shaped mirror keeps its layout.
phoneApp: No changes in this release: 0.8.2 is still the current phone app.

releases.title: Agents that don't trip
releases.summary: Coding agents act on settled screens, find what they're told to press, and never report a change that didn't happen.
mac: Every agent action returns only after the screen settles, so the next step never lands mid-transition.
tap_element and set_text keep looking for up to 2.5 s while menus and pages open.
A plain label presses the row or button around it; rows without text are named by the text inside them.
set_text reads the field back, falls back to clear-and-type, and reports what the field shows if it still doesn't match.
scroll says whether the content moved, and scrolls the list directly when a drag does nothing.
Element trees leave out the keyboard and the status and navigation bars (system: true brings them back).
unlock_phone answers an app's PIN or fingerprint prompt on the phone's screen, still only after Touch ID.
About and What's new pages in Settings.
phoneApp: Tells the Mac when a screen has finished changing, per display.
Names clickable rows that have no text of their own.
About and What's new pages in Settings.

releases.title: Updates by themselves
releases.summary: Both apps now update without a trip to GitHub, and a forgotten Mac is one tap away from linking again.
mac: Updates itself: checks for new releases, verifies the download's SHA-256, swaps the app in place and reopens.
Carries the newest phone app and offers it when a connected phone has an older one.
Links a phone again as soon as the phone allows it, without re-plugging.
Settings → Phone app always offers Pair or Relink.
phoneApp: Update available on Home: installed by the Mac in Developer mode, downloaded from the Mac over Wi-Fi otherwise. The phone app never goes online for it.
Link now and Link again on Home after a forget; the forgotten Mac is named, with Pair again in Wi-Fi mode.

releases.title: First release
releases.summary: Mirror and control Android phones from your Mac over USB, wireless debugging or plain Wi-Fi.
mac: Hardware-decoded mirroring with mouse, keyboard, clipboard, drag and drop, screenshots and recordings.
Second screens: independent virtual displays of the same phone, each in its own window.
Unlock with a saved PIN, protected by Touch ID.
MCP server with 42 tools for coding agents, working on their own second screen.
Wi-Fi, no setup: pair a phone with a QR code and mirror over an encrypted link, no developer options.
Install from the terminal or with Homebrew.
phoneApp: Wi-Fi mirroring without developer mode (screen capture, hardware H.264, AES-256-GCM).
Control from the Mac through accessibility; QR pairing; two-way forget.
Device details in 12 groups, Share to Mac from any app, element access for agents on any display.
